metadata.title: The role of knowledge-rich curricula in promoting deep thinking and complex skill acquisition

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This manuscript is a conceptual/theoretical synthesis of prior research and policy examples; it does not report an original student-level large-scale assessment dataset analysis. As a result, there is no described sampling frame, no analytic subsample construction from TIMSS/PISA/PIRLS microdata, and no application of complex survey weights or replicate-weight procedures. The paper discusses external assessment trends (e.g., TIMSS and PISA) at a descriptive/policy level rather than estimating model-based student outcomes from ILSA microdata. Therefore, no ILSA weight variable (e.g., student design weights or BRR/JRR) is specified for statistical inference.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: Plausible Values (PV) handling is not applicable because the paper does not conduct an empirical analysis of ILSA cognitive achievement outcomes using PV-based scoring. Instead, it provides a narrative argument and summarizes findings from prior studies and policy contexts (e.g., knowledge-rich curricula) without fitting PV-based achievement models on student microdata. Missing-data handling is not reported because there is no original dataset construction or statistical modeling pipeline that would require specifying how missing values were treated.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: No original ILSA microdata sample is analyzed. The paper synthesizes prior empirical studies (including experiments and longitudinal work) and discusses national policy changes using descriptive references to external assessment trends (e.g., PISA/TIMSS) rather than reporting an analytic subsample derived from a specific ILSA dataset.

data.null_fields_interpretation: The extraction is sparse because the manuscript does not present an original empirical analysis of ILSA microdata. It contains no reported ML models, no PV handling, no missing-data strategy, and no student-level sampling/weighting details; it instead provides a theoretical argument and summarizes findings from other studies and policy contexts. Consequently, fields that would normally be populated for an empirical predictive paper (countries with n, total_students, main_findings with metrics) are intentionally left empty.
